name: BPC-157
blurb: A stable gastric pentadecapeptide widely studied for tissue repair.
mechanism: A synthetic 15-amino-acid fragment of a gastric protein studied for promoting angiogenesis (new blood-vessel formation) and tissue repair in preclinical models.
receptors: Acts largely through growth-factor and nitric-oxide pathways; no single named receptor — modulates the VEGFR2 / NO system.
research: Extensively studied in vitro and in animal models for tendon, ligament, muscle and gut-lining repair.

name: TB-500
blurb: The active fragment of Thymosin Beta-4, studied for cell migration and repair.
mechanism: A synthetic fragment of Thymosin Beta-4 that binds and regulates actin, supporting cell migration and tissue repair in preclinical work.
receptors: No classical receptor — acts intracellularly via actin sequestration.
research: Studied in models of wound healing, cardiac repair and flexibility of connective tissue.

name: BPC-157 & TB-500
blurb: A blended pair frequently studied together for repair research.
mechanism: Combines BPC-157 (angiogenesis/repair) with TB-500 (actin-mediated cell migration) — two complementary repair pathways.
research: Researched together for soft-tissue and connective-tissue repair models.

name: CJC-1295 (no DAC)
blurb: A GHRH analogue studied for pulsatile growth-hormone release.
mechanism: A modified fragment of growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH 1-29) that stimulates the pituitary to release growth hormone in preclinical models.
research: Frequently studied alongside ghrelin-receptor agonists (e.g. Ipamorelin) for synergistic GH release.

name: Ipamorelin
blurb: One of the most selective growth-hormone secretagogues studied.
mechanism: A pentapeptide that selectively activates the ghrelin receptor to prompt GH release with little effect on cortisol or prolactin in preclinical models.
research: Studied as a clean tool for isolating GH-secretagogue signalling; often paired with CJC-1295.

name: Sermorelin
mechanism: The first 29 amino acids of GHRH; stimulates pituitary GH release in preclinical models.
research: A long-studied reference GHRH analogue for growth-axis research.

name: Tesamorelin
blurb: A stabilised GHRH analogue with extended activity.
mechanism: A GHRH analogue modified for greater stability, studied for sustained GH-axis stimulation in preclinical models.
research: Researched for visceral-fat and metabolic endpoints in the literature.

name: GHRP-6
mechanism: A hexapeptide that stimulates GH release via the ghrelin receptor, with broader hormonal effects than Ipamorelin.
research: A widely cited reference GHRP in growth-axis research.

name: Hexarelin
mechanism: A synthetic hexapeptide GH secretagogue acting at the ghrelin receptor, studied for potent GH release.
research: Studied for GH release and cardiac-tissue effects in preclinical models.

name: GHK-Cu
blurb: A copper-binding tripeptide central to skin-repair research.
mechanism: A naturally occurring tripeptide that binds copper and is studied for collagen synthesis, antioxidant and skin-remodelling activity in fibroblast models.
receptors: No single receptor — acts via copper delivery and gene-expression modulation.
research: One of the most-studied cosmetic peptides for skin firmness and repair in vitro.

name: GHK
blurb: The copper-free parent tripeptide of GHK-Cu.
mechanism: The base tripeptide that chelates copper to form GHK-Cu; studied for skin and repair signalling.
receptors: Acts via copper binding / gene modulation.
research: The reference parent compound for GHK-Cu research.

name: KPV
mechanism: The C-terminal tripeptide of α-MSH, studied for anti-inflammatory activity in gut and skin models.
research: Researched for inflammatory-bowel and skin-inflammation models in vitro.

name: Semax
blurb: A nootropic peptide studied for neuroprotection.
mechanism: A synthetic ACTH(4-10) fragment analogue studied for BDNF modulation and neuroprotection in preclinical models.
receptors: Melanocortin / BDNF-linked pathways (no single classical receptor).
research: Studied for cognition, focus and neuroprotection in animal models.

name: Selank
blurb: An anxiolytic-studied peptide derived from tuftsin.
mechanism: A synthetic analogue of the immunopeptide tuftsin, studied for anxiolytic and immunomodulatory activity in preclinical models.
research: Researched for stress, anxiety and immune-modulation models.

name: DSIP
blurb: A nonapeptide studied for sleep and stress modulation.
mechanism: A naturally occurring nonapeptide studied for delta-wave sleep promotion and stress-axis modulation in preclinical work.
receptors: Not fully characterised — modulates several neuroendocrine pathways.
research: Researched for sleep architecture and stress-hormone endpoints.

name: Epitalon
blurb: A tetrapeptide studied for telomerase and longevity research.
mechanism: A synthetic tetrapeptide studied for telomerase activation and circadian/pineal regulation in preclinical models.
receptors: Acts on gene expression / pineal pathways — no classical receptor.
research: A widely cited longevity-research peptide in vitro and in animal studies.

name: MOTS-c
blurb: A mitochondrial-derived peptide studied for metabolism.
mechanism: A 16-amino-acid mitochondrial-derived peptide studied for AMPK activation and metabolic regulation in preclinical models.
research: Researched for insulin sensitivity, exercise and metabolic endpoints.

name: NAD+
blurb: A core cellular coenzyme studied for energy and longevity.
mechanism: A coenzyme central to mitochondrial energy metabolism and sirtuin activity; studied for cellular energy and ageing research.
receptors: Coenzyme / sirtuin & PARP substrate (not a peptide receptor).
research: Extensively studied for metabolism, DNA repair and longevity pathways.

name: Glutathione
mechanism: A tripeptide (Glu-Cys-Gly) central to cellular antioxidant defence and detoxification, studied in oxidative-stress models.
research: One of the most-studied antioxidants in cell biology.

name: Melanotan II
blurb: A melanocortin agonist studied for pigmentation.
mechanism: A cyclic analogue of α-MSH studied for melanogenesis (pigment production) via melanocortin receptors in preclinical models.
research: Researched for pigmentation and melanocortin-pathway endpoints.

name: PT-141
blurb: A melanocortin agonist fragment of Melanotan II.
mechanism: A metabolite of Melanotan II studied for central melanocortin-receptor activity (MC4R) in preclinical models.
research: Researched for melanocortin-pathway and behavioural endpoints.

name: Thymosin Alpha-1
mechanism: A 28-amino-acid thymic peptide studied for T-cell maturation and immune modulation in preclinical and clinical literature.
research: Widely studied as an immune-modulator reference peptide.

name: Retatrutide
mechanism: A single peptide that activates three incretin receptors (GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon), studied for metabolic regulation in the literature.
research: A leading subject of metabolic-research interest for combined incretin action.

name: Tirzepatide
mechanism: A single peptide activating both GIP and GLP-1 receptors, studied for metabolic and incretin research.
research: Widely studied for combined incretin-pathway metabolic effects.

name: Semaglutide
mechanism: A GLP-1 analogue modified for extended half-life, studied extensively for incretin/metabolic endpoints.
research: One of the most-studied single-incretin agonists in the literature.

name: AOD-9604
blurb: A growth-hormone fragment studied for lipolysis.
mechanism: A synthetic fragment of human growth hormone (176-191) studied for fat-metabolism (lipolysis) without the full GH effects in preclinical models.
receptors: Acts on lipid-metabolism pathways; not a classical GH-receptor agonist.
research: Researched for fat-metabolism endpoints in animal models.

name: GHRP-2
mechanism: A synthetic hexapeptide GH secretagogue acting at the ghrelin receptor; more potent but less selective than Ipamorelin.
research: A widely cited GH-secretagogue reference; raises GH alongside some cortisol/prolactin in models.

name: IGF-1 LR3
mechanism: An 83-amino-acid IGF-1 analogue with reduced binding-protein affinity, giving extended activity in preclinical models.
research: Studied for cell proliferation and growth-signalling in vitro.

name: IGF-1 DES
blurb: A truncated, highly potent IGF-1 variant.
mechanism: IGF-1 missing its first three residues, with very low binding-protein affinity and strong local IGF-1R activity in models.
research: Researched for localised growth-signalling endpoints.

name: MGF
blurb: A splice variant of IGF-1 linked to mechanical load.
mechanism: The C-terminal E-domain peptide of a mechano-sensitive IGF-1 splice variant, studied for muscle satellite-cell activation.
receptors: Distinct from IGF-1R — acts via its own E-peptide signalling.
research: Studied for muscle repair and hypertrophy models.

name: Thymosin Beta-4
blurb: The full 43-residue actin-regulating peptide (TB-500 is its fragment).
mechanism: A 43-amino-acid peptide that sequesters actin to drive cell migration, angiogenesis and tissue repair in preclinical models.
receptors: No classical receptor — intracellular actin regulation.
research: Parent peptide to TB-500; studied for wound, cardiac and corneal repair.

name: Humanin
mechanism: A 24-amino-acid mitochondrial-derived peptide studied for cytoprotection and metabolic signalling in preclinical models.
receptors: Acts via formyl-peptide and gp130 receptor systems.
research: Researched for neuroprotection and metabolic-ageing endpoints.

name: SS-31
mechanism: A tetrapeptide that binds cardiolipin on the inner mitochondrial membrane, studied for restoring mitochondrial efficiency.
receptors: Cardiolipin (membrane target) — not a cell-surface receptor.
research: Studied for mitochondrial-dysfunction and oxidative-stress models.

name: Matrixyl
mechanism: A lipidated fragment of collagen (KTTKS) studied for stimulating collagen and matrix synthesis in skin fibroblasts.
receptors: Acts as a matrikine signalling fragment — no single receptor.
research: One of the most-studied cosmetic anti-wrinkle peptides in vitro.

name: Argireline
mechanism: A hexapeptide studied for modulating SNARE-complex-mediated neurotransmitter release in expression-line cosmetic research.
research: Widely studied as a topical expression-line research peptide.

name: SNAP-8
mechanism: An octapeptide extension of Argireline studied for SNARE-modulation in expression-line cosmetic research.
research: Researched as a longer, higher-affinity Argireline analogue.

name: AHK-Cu
blurb: A copper peptide studied for hair and skin.
mechanism: A copper-binding tripeptide studied for follicle and skin support, related to GHK-Cu.
research: Researched for hair-follicle and skin-remodelling endpoints.

name: Kisspeptin-10
mechanism: A 10-amino-acid fragment of kisspeptin studied for stimulating GnRH release via KISS1R in preclinical models.
research: Studied for reproductive-axis and hormone-release endpoints.

name: Gonadorelin
mechanism: The decapeptide that triggers pituitary release of LH and FSH; studied as the reference reproductive-axis trigger.
research: A long-standing reference peptide for reproductive-axis research.

name: LL-37
mechanism: A 37-residue cathelicidin-derived peptide studied for antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activity in vitro.
research: A heavily studied reference antimicrobial peptide.

name: Melanotan I
mechanism: A linear α-MSH analogue studied for melanogenesis via MC1R, more receptor-selective than Melanotan II.
research: Researched for photoprotection and pigmentation endpoints.

name: Alpha-MSH
mechanism: A 13-amino-acid melanocortin hormone studied for pigmentation and anti-inflammatory melanocortin signalling.
research: The reference melanocortin agonist; parent of MT-I/MT-II and KPV.

name: Liraglutide
mechanism: An acylated GLP-1 analogue with extended half-life, studied for incretin/metabolic endpoints.
research: A widely studied single-incretin agonist reference.

name: Exenatide
blurb: A GLP-1 receptor agonist from exendin-4.
mechanism: A 39-amino-acid GLP-1R agonist (exendin-4) studied for incretin/metabolic research.
research: A long-studied incretin-pathway reference peptide.

name: Glucagon
mechanism: A 29-amino-acid hormone that raises blood glucose and mobilises energy stores; the glucagon arm of triple agonists.
research: A reference hormone for metabolic and incretin-combination research.

name: GIP
blurb: An incretin hormone; the GIP arm of dual/triple agonists.
mechanism: A 42-amino-acid incretin hormone studied for insulin secretion and the GIP arm of combination agonists.
research: A reference incretin for dual/triple-agonist research (e.g. Tirzepatide, Retatrutide).

name: Cagrilintide
mechanism: An acylated amylin analogue studied for satiety/metabolic endpoints, often paired with GLP-1 agonists in the literature.
research: Researched for combined amylin + incretin metabolic effects.

name: Survodutide
mechanism: A single peptide activating GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, studied for metabolic endpoints.
research: A subject of dual-incretin metabolic research.

name: Mazdutide
mechanism: A single peptide activating GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, studied for metabolic endpoints.
research: A subject of dual-incretin metabolic research.

name: Pinealon
blurb: A short peptide bioregulator studied for the brain.
mechanism: A tripeptide (Glu-Asp-Arg) studied for neuroprotection and gene-expression regulation in preclinical models.
receptors: Acts on gene expression — no classical receptor.
research: Researched for cognition and oxidative-stress endpoints.

name: Vilon
mechanism: A dipeptide (Lys-Glu) studied for immune and gene-regulatory effects in preclinical longevity research.
research: Studied in the short-peptide-bioregulator literature.

name: Vesugen
blurb: A short peptide bioregulator studied for vasculature.
mechanism: A tripeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp) studied for vascular gene-regulation in preclinical longevity research.
research: Studied in the short-peptide-bioregulator literature.

name: Thymulin
blurb: A thymic peptide studied for immune balance.
mechanism: A zinc-dependent thymic nonapeptide studied for T-cell modulation in preclinical models.
research: Researched as an immune-modulator reference peptide.

name: Adipotide
blurb: A targeting peptide studied for fat-vasculature.
mechanism: A pro-apoptotic peptide (CKGGRAKDC motif) studied for targeting the blood supply of adipose tissue in animal models.
research: Researched for adiposity endpoints in preclinical models.

name: Oxytocin
mechanism: A cyclic nonapeptide hormone studied for social-bonding and smooth-muscle signalling in preclinical models.
research: A widely studied neuropeptide reference.

name: Vasopressin
mechanism: A cyclic nonapeptide studied for water balance and vascular tone via vasopressin receptors.
research: A reference neuroendocrine peptide.
